extra_misconceptions.fact: Genetic evidence confirms that all domestic dogs descended exclusively from ancient Eurasian gray wolves over 15,000 years ago.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: All modern domestic dog breeds descended from multiple wild canine species including foxes, coyotes, and jackals.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The Non-Sporting group is a diverse collection of breeds with varied histories, such as Poodles, Dalmatians, and Bulldogs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dogs in the AKC Non-Sporting group share a single historical working job like hunting or livestock guarding.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Terriers were bred in the British Isles to dig into burrows and dispatch foxes, badgers, and rats with high tenacity.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Terrier breeds were originally developed as quiet lapdogs rather than independent vermin hunters.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Toy breeds retain alert companion instincts and still need structured daily walks, play, and obedience training.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Purebred dogs registered in the Toy group have lower energy needs and require no daily mental stimulation.

extra_socratic_questions: What evolutionary advantage drove early gray wolves to live near Paleolithic human camps?
Which physical traits and hunting styles distinguish Sighthounds from Scenthounds in the Hound group?
Why do Sporting group dogs typically have water-resistant coats and soft mouths for carrying game?
Under what working conditions were Herding group breeds separated from the broader Working group?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Official canine height is measured vertically from level ground to the top of the withers, the highest point of the shoulders.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Standing height on a dog is measured from the ground to the top of the head when the neck is raised.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The canine hock corresponds to the human ankle and heel, while the true knee is the forward-bending stifle joint higher up.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The hock joint on a dog's back leg bends backward because it is an inverted canine knee joint.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Foreleg dewclaws are functional vestigial thumbs attached by tendons that help stabilize the wrist during sharp turns.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Dewclaws on the inner forelegs are useless skin growths that have no bone or tendon attachments.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Flews are the pendulous upper lips of a dog, which are especially prominent in breeds like Bloodhounds and Boxers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A dog's flews are the fleshy pads on the bottom of the paws that absorb shock during running.

extra_socratic_questions: Where are the withers located on a dog, and why is that landmark used to measure standing height?
Which joint on a dog's hind leg corresponds anatomically to the human knee and contains a kneecap?
What is the anatomical difference between a dog's pastern on the foreleg and the hock on the hind leg?
Which facial landmark sits directly between the muzzle and the skull at the inner corners of the eyes?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Delayed punishment only makes a puppy fearful of its owner; effective house-training relies on frequent trips outside and rewards.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rubbing a puppy's nose in an indoor accident teaches the dog to associate the mess with going outside.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An oversized crate lets a puppy soil one corner and sleep in another; use a divider so the space only fits standing and turning.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Buying an extra-large wire crate for a small puppy prevents indoor accidents during house-training.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Proper socialization involves calm, controlled, positive exposures to new people, animals, sights, and sounds during puppyhood.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Socialization training simply means letting an off-leash puppy run into a crowded dog park with adult dogs.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Families must match a breed's adult size, daily exercise demands, grooming needs, and temperament to their living space and schedule.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Selecting a dog breed based solely on coat appearance or movie popularity guarantees a good family match.

extra_socratic_questions: Why does crate training help speed up house-training for a young puppy when sized properly?
What happens to a puppy's confidence if it is not exposed to varied people, sounds, and surfaces early?
Which household factors should a family evaluate before adopting a high-drive herding or working breed?
What role do municipal leash laws and microchip registration play in responsible neighborhood pet ownership?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Free-feeding promotes obesity and hides sudden appetite loss; measured meals at scheduled times allow exact tracking in your log.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Leaving a full bowl of kibble out all day is the most accurate way to track a dog's daily caloric intake.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Human shampoo has the wrong pH for canine skin and strips natural oils, causing dry, irritated skin; use dog-formulated shampoo.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Bathing a dog every few days with human soap keeps its skin healthier and eliminates shedding.

extra_misconceptions.fact: You can weigh a dog at home by weighing yourself holding the dog and subtracting your own weight, then logging the difference.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Weighing a large dog requires a specialized clinic scale because home bathroom scales cannot be used.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Each dog nail contains a living blood vessel and nerve called the quick, which bleeds and hurts if clipped too short.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Trimming a dog's nails flush with the toe pad is safe because canine nails contain only dead keratin.

extra_socratic_questions: What physical indicators on a dog's ribs and waist confirm a healthy weight alongside your weekly scale log?
Why is it dangerous to bathe a dog too frequently with human shampoo during your two-month care period?
What trend in your daily feeding and weekly weight log would signal that your dog needs a veterinary checkup?
Which grooming tools and nail-trimming precautions prevent cutting the blood vessel inside a dog's nail?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Repeating a cue teaches the dog to ignore the first command; say the command once clearly, then guide and reward the behavior.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Repeating a verbal command like 'sit, sit, sit' louder helps an untrained dog understand the word faster.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Retractable leashes reward pulling by extending under tension and can cause cord burns; a standard 6-foot flat leash gives clear control.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Retractable cord leashes are ideal for basic obedience training because they give the dog room to roam.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Short, upbeat training sessions of 5 to 15 minutes held once or twice daily prevent boredom and improve canine retention.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Training sessions should last at least an hour at a time so the dog does not forget the new commands.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Forcing jaws open triggers resource guarding; teach 'drop it' by trading the held item for a higher-value treat on cue.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Prying a dog's jaws open by force is the best way to teach the 'drop it' obedience command.

extra_socratic_questions: Why must a reward or verbal marker be delivered within two seconds of the dog completing a command?
What is the difference in safety and control between a flat 6-foot training leash and a retractable leash?
Where should your dog's shoulders align relative to your left leg when executing a proper heel command?
Why should you never call your dog using the 'come' command if you plan to scold or punish it upon arrival?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Maternal antibodies can block early vaccines, so puppies require a booster series through 16 weeks followed by adult boosters.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: One puppy vaccination shot at six weeks of age provides lifelong immunity against parvovirus and distemper.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Heartworm larvae are transmitted exclusively through the bite of an infected mosquito and mature inside the heart and lung arteries.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Heartworms pass directly from one dog to another through shared water bowls or contact with infected feces.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dry kibble shatters on contact and does not clean below the gumline; regular brushing with canine toothpaste is needed to stop tartar.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Chewing on hard dry kibble alone scrapes away all subgingival plaque and prevents canine periodontal disease.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dogs swallow toothpaste, and human formulas contain fluoride, detergents, and sometimes xylitol, which causes toxic liver failure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Human toothpaste is safe for brushing a dog's teeth because dogs spit out the foam after brushing.

extra_socratic_questions: Why do puppies need a series of booster vaccinations every 3 to 4 weeks rather than a single shot at birth?
What vector transmits heartworms to dogs, and why is monthly prevention safer than treating an active infection?
Why is it dangerous to brush a dog's teeth with human fluoride or xylitol toothpaste instead of canine paste?
Which core vaccines are required or recommended for almost all dogs regardless of regional lifestyle?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Even the gentlest dog may reflexively snap or bite out of fear and pain when injured, so approach calmly and muzzle if safe.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A friendly family dog will never bite its owner when in severe pain after being hit by a car.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Never muzzle a dog that is vomiting, having difficulty breathing, suffering heatstroke, or has a severe facial or jaw injury.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every injured dog should be muzzled immediately, even if it is vomiting, choking, or gasping for air.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An overly tight bandage cuts off circulation and causes tissue death; you should be able to slip two fingers under the wrap.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wrapping an elastic bandage as tightly as possible around a bleeding leg is the safest way to leave it overnight.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Strong alcohol and peroxide damage healthy healing tissue; flush minor wounds gently with clean water or sterile saline instead.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pouring undiluted rubbing alcohol or hydrogen peroxide deep into a puncture wound speeds up canine healing.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what medical conditions must you never place an emergency gauze muzzle on an injured dog?
Where should the initial loop of an emergency muzzle knot be tied before securing it behind the dog's ears?
What physical check confirms that a paw or leg bandage is not wrapped so tightly that it cuts off circulation?
What technique safely moves a dog hit by a car onto a flat board or blanket stretcher to protect its spine?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Shelters quarantine new arrivals for a stray hold and medical exam to check for microchips, parasites, and contagious diseases.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Animal shelters place newly arrived stray dogs directly into shared group runs with adoptable pets.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Canine parvovirus resists plain water and many cleaners; facilities must use veterinary-grade disinfectants with proper contact time.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hosing down kennel floors with plain water is sufficient to kill canine parvovirus between shelter animals.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Credentialed veterinary technicians perform lab diagnostics, take X-rays, monitor anesthesia, and assist in surgical procedures.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Veterinary technicians only clean cages and hold leashes during a veterinary hospital appointment.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unvaccinated puppies face high infection risk in high-turnover facilities; shelters require full vaccinations before dog-to-dog introductions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Bringing your own unvaccinated puppy into an animal shelter kennel area is a safe way to pick out a playmate.

extra_socratic_questions: Why do veterinary hospitals and shelters maintain strict isolation wards away from general boarding kennels?
What sanitation and biosecurity steps prevent staff from spreading parvovirus or kennel cough between cages?
What medical and behavioral checks do animal shelters perform on a stray dog before clearing it for adoption?
Which diagnostic and surgical rooms in a veterinary clinic require sterile protocols similar to human hospitals?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rabies vaccination is a prerequisite, but owners must separately register with the city or county clerk to obtain a valid license.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A veterinarian's metal rabies vaccination tag automatically serves as a valid municipal dog license in local jurisdictions.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many municipal ordinances define legal restraint by the maximum possible extension of the lead or ban retractable cords outright.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A 16-foot retractable cord leash complies with municipal six-foot leash ordinances as long as the thumb brake stays locked.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Municipal licensing and rabies vaccination mandates apply to all dogs above the statutory age threshold regardless of yard confinement.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A dog that stays inside a fenced residential yard all year is legally exempt from county rabies vaccination and licensing laws.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Uncollected dog feces wash roundworm eggs, parvovirus, and coliform bacteria into storm drains, violating sanitation ordinances.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Leaving canine waste in a grassy park ditch is harmless to the neighborhood because rainwater quickly washes it into the soil.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to bypass the 10-day quarantine observation period after a domestic dog bites a neighbor?
What legal distinction separates a veterinarian's rabies vaccination certificate from an active municipal dog license tag?
What measurement confirms that your walking lead complies with a municipal six-foot maximum leash ordinance on public trails?
Under what condition does an electronic voice-control collar fail to satisfy a strict physical-restraint municipal leash law?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Only a licensed Doctor of Veterinary Medicine may diagnose disease, prescribe drugs, or perform surgery under state practice acts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Credentialed veterinary technicians can legally diagnose illnesses, prescribe medications, and perform surgery without a veterinarian.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A board-certified veterinary behaviorist must earn a veterinary degree and complete a residency approved by the ACVB.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Any experienced dog trainer can legally call themselves a veterinary behaviorist after passing a basic obedience certification exam.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Candidates for the CPDT-KA exam must log at least 300 hours of hands-on dog training experience within the preceding three years.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Becoming a certified professional dog trainer requires zero documented hands-on hours before sitting for the national credential exam.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most wilderness search-and-rescue K-9 handlers serve as unpaid volunteers who personally fund their dog's gear, travel, and vet care.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Search-and-rescue canine handlers are always paid full-time salaries with all dog medical and gear expenses covered by local police.

extra_socratic_questions: Which clinical responsibilities separate a licensed veterinarian from a credentialed veterinary technician in a hospital?
What logged documentation confirms that an aspiring dog trainer has met the 300-hour experience requirement for CPDT-KA testing?
What happens to a mobile groomer's net salary projection when liability insurance and equipment maintenance expenses are omitted?
Why is it dangerous to evaluate an unfamiliar shelter intake dog before verifying slip-lead security and isolation PPE readiness?
